“One of the towers of the Financial Center in Riyadh was targeted in a terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia, causing material damage but no injuries -praise be to God,” the Saudi authorities said in a statement released on Thursday.

The press release included an image showing notable but relatively minor damage to the PIF headquarters. Video footage appeared to show a missile slamming into the 80-storey tower, but Middle East Eye could not independently verify the footage.

Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] The enduring influence of Christian Zionism in Brazil
item.description:
The enduring influence of Christian Zionism in Brazil

Submitted by Ana Maria Monjardino on Thu, 11/19/2026 - 09:29
Despite Flavio Bolsonaro’s defeat, Bolsonarismo, a right-wing ideology that promotes religious nationalism and Christian Zionism, retains considerable influence in Congress
A believer wrapped in an Israeli flag takes part in the "March for Jesus", an event that gathers a wide range of evangelical congregations, in Sao Paulo, Brazil on 19 June 2025 (AFP)
Off

The presidential victory of Brazil’s Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, or Lula, disrupted the rise of Latin America’s far right, for which subordination to US interests and diplomatic rapprochement with Israel is the order of the day. 

It was a significant win. However the Brazilian far right has not disappeared.

Despite Flavio Bolsonaro’s defeat and the criminal conviction of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, the Bolsonarist Liberal Party became the largest in both houses of Congress. This reflects the enduring influence of Bolsonarismo, a right-wing ideology that promotes militarism, religious nationalism and Christian Zionism. 

“I categorise Christian Zionism under the umbrella of religious nationalism,” said Ronilso Pacheco, a Brazilian theologian. “I do not view it as a separate, detached offshoot, but rather as an additional, interconnected front.”

In fact, “our evangelical fundamentalism is deeply Judaising and is committed to the unconditional defence of Israel. If this movement advances, Christian Zionism advances right along with it,” he told Middle East Eye.

This symbiosis is rooted in the manufactured theological connection between Israel and evangelicalism, particularly Pentecostalism. It is inseparable from the arrival of US and European Pentecostals in the early 20th century and the proselytising missions of the Cold War, which brought waves of evangelical missionaries, alongside clandestine CIA operations “directed at competing with communism”. 

Although not their strategic goal, the biblical teachings they espoused laid the groundwork for modern Christian Zionism. 

The General Convention of the Assemblies of God, for example, founded by Swedish missionaries in 1911, is now Brazil’s largest Pentecostal megachurch. Its declaration of faith draws heavily on the Book of Revelation, promoting the Christian Zionist belief that the presence of Jewish people in Israel is a precursor to the End Times and the Second Coming of Christ. 

And it is not alone. Across Brazil, powerful networks of megachurches, political caucuses and lobbying groups eagerly exploit evangelical fervour by manipulating biblical scripture to invigorate political support for the far right and the State of Israel, as inseparable entities, in the name of God. 

The imaginary Israel 

“Israeli flags, menorahs, tallitot, and kippahs are incorporated into religious services and celebrations, as though supporting the Israeli state were an obligation of Christian faith,” explained Rawa Alsagheer, a Palestinian-Syrian filmmaker and coordinator with Samidoun in Brazil. 

This has been quite common in Brazil since the 1990s, explained Pacheco, “rooted in the notion of ‘blessing Israel to be blessed’ and the fixed idea of ​​the ‘chosen people’.”

Blessings theology is based on Genesis 12:3, a biblical verse in which God tells Abraham: "I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse.”

According to Christian Zionism, which designates Jewish people as the only physical descendants of Abraham and the distinct heirs to a national and territorial promised land, that covenant applies to the entire Zionist state. 

Silas Malafaia, one of the best-known Christian Zionists and televangelists in Brazil, referenced the same theology during an interview with BBC News Brazil in 2019.

“It is there in the book of Genesis,” he said. “We believe that when a nation blesses Israel, it is blessed. We believe this as a principle of faith.” 

Yet “this perspective fails to distinguish the political State of Israel from biblical Israel,” argued Pacheco. That conflation, he noted, constitutes what Professor Michel Gherman termed “the imaginary Israel”. 

Echoing the same sentiments, Rene Terra Nova, founder of the International Restoration Ministries and national director of the International Christian Embassy Jerusalem in Brazil, has guided his followers “onto the path of blessing” by mobilising tens of thousands of Brazilians to visit Jerusalem for the annual Feast of Tabernacles.

This “tireless work in spreading the love for Israel” also includes organising a weekly shabbat and flamboyant pro-Israel messaging on his social media. 

Upon those foundations, Brazilian Christian Zionism is growing and evolving, with 7 October 2023 serving as a catalyst, “a moment where a threat faced by the State of Israel, or the Israeli people, transformed into a conservative rallying cry,” Pacheco explained. 

Brazil’s Catholic population has declined from 82.9 percent in 1992 to 56.7 percent in the 2022 census, according to the national statistics institute (IBGE). Over the same period, the evangelical population grew from 9 percent to 26.9 percent, meaning more than one in four Brazilians now identifies as evangelical.

Megachurch monopoly 

While their followers wait dutifully for their blessings, the upper echelons of Christian Zionist pastors reap significant financial rewards. 

Edir Macedo is a Pentecostal bishop, billionaire and founder of the Universal Kingdom of God (UCKG) who was listed on the Israel Allies Foundation’s “top 50 Israel allies 2022”.

'Our evangelical fundamentalism is deeply Judaising and is committed to the unconditional defence of Israel'

- Ronilso Pacheco, a Brazilian theologian

He is also credited for building the Temple of Solomon in Sao Paulo, an ostentatious homage to Israel where menorahs adorn the walls and the building itself is made from $8bn worth of stone imported from the occupied West Bank city of Hebron. 

Macedo “has undergone a profound process of ‘Judaisation’, perhaps the most extensive among the country’s major Pentecostal leaders,” said Pacheco. “It is an immersion that spans everything from religious attire to the precise, faithful reproduction of biblical dimensions for the temple and its sacred vessels.”  

UCKG now has congregations in over 100 countries, with approximately 5,000 churches and missionary centres in Brazil alone. Business is subsequently fruitful and Macedo, who also owns Brazil’s second largest commercial broadcasting station, RecordTV, is one of the richest religious leaders in the world with a net worth of $1.8bn. 

Telenovelas such as Apocalypse, produced by Record TV, are also filled with pro-Israel propaganda.

Apocalypse, which “draws inspiration from the biblical book of Revelation” is “marked by clear dispensationalist and Christian Zionist themes,” wrote Professor Manoela Carpenedo, whose work focuses on grassroots Christian movements.

“The telenovela is focused on the period of the ‘Great Tribulation’, where the antichrist reigns for seven years, and good Christians are taken up to heaven during the Rapture while others endure tragic events,” Manoela wrote. 

Christian Zionism permeates Brazilian life. It is even evident in pop-gospel music, such as Aline Barros’ “Como Israel” and Fernandinho’s “Yeshua”, which was produced in collaboration with the Israel-based “worship movement” and record label, Maoz Israel Music.  

Proselytising politics

Aside from its cultural impact, it has had a huge effect on Brazilian politics, enabling the rise of a fervently pro-Israel bloc in Congress. “We must understand the political meaning of this operation,” said Alsagheer. After all, “Zionism did not emerge from a biblical prophecy.” 

Congressional groups like The Israel Allies Caucus and the Evangelical Parliamentary Front foster ties between Christian Zionist faith leaders and lawmakers. Last month, Israel Allies Foundation president, Josh Reinstein, even endorsed Flavio Bolsonaro, posting a picture of the two of them under a reference to Genesis 12:3. 

During his campaign trail, Flavio promised to “defend the right of Israel to survive”, confirming “full support” for Israeli settlers in the West Bank and pledging to relocate the Brazilian embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem if elected.

Despite his monumental loss, the enduring influence of Bolsonarismo including the role of his stepmother, Senator-elect Michelle Bolsonaro, should not be overlooked.

A devout evangelical with a blue Star of David tattooed on her arm, Michelle Bolsonaro played a critical role galvanising evangelical women in support of her husband, Jair, during the 2022 presidential race, once referring to his following as an “army of God”. Her Instagram is also peppered with biblical verses and Israeli flag emojis. 

The Evangelical Parliamentary Front, an unofficial congressional caucus of Christian lawmakers led by Gilberto Nascimento, has also played a central role in fostering pro-Israel rhetoric and policies.

In May 2018, the caucus organised a parliamentary session celebrating the creation of Israel, or the Nakba, during which 750,000 Palestinians were forcibly displaced.

The leader of the session, Hidekazu Takayama, made yet another reference to Genesis 13:12, discussed lobbying efforts to relocate the Brazilian embassy to Jerusalem and spoke at length about Israel’s technological assets.

“Any criticism of Israel, or of its project to take full control of Gaza, as well as any assertion that Israel is carrying out an ongoing genocide against the Palestinians, will undoubtedly be met with unanimous rejection by the caucus,” explained Pacheco, adding: “We have seen this happen several times.” 

Of course, the alliance between Israel and Brazil, Zionism and right-wing evangelicalism is not sustained by religion alone.

“It involves military, economic, technological, diplomatic, and ideological interests,” said Alsagheer.

As a result, even conservative Catholic lawmakers who recognise the strategic political and material potential of supporting Israel are keen to adopt the rhetoric. This was most famously demonstrated by the former president and leader of the Bolsonarist clan, but others, including Sao Paulo Governor Tarcisio de Freitas, have followed suit. 

Because “support for Israel is not a secondary issue for this political sector,” explained Alsagheer. “It is part of its political project.”

item.description:
Why Britain must oppose UN candidacy of UAE's Nusseibeh

Submitted by Monica Harding on Thu, 11/19/2026 - 14:25
The Emirati diplomat has repeatedly denied her country's involvement in fuelling Sudan's bloody war
Emirati diplomat and minister Lana Nusseibeh, now a candidate for the position of UN secretary general, attends a meeting in Manama, Bahrain, on 25 June 2026 (Eric Lee/AFP)
Off

The United Arab Emirates is a small country but a very rich one, so the British government may be all too often afraid to utter a word of criticism. 

No matter that the UK is working to end the horrific war in Sudan, while the UAE is reportedly fuelling it with weapons and mercenaries. The UK government confines itself to vague statements about unnamed “external backers” of the conflict in Sudan - the world’s biggest humanitarian crisis.

The UAE is nominating one of its diplomats to become UN secretary general. Lana Nusseibeh is a loyal spokesperson for her country, dismissing even the UN’s own findings that her government backs the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a Sudanese armed group that has committed atrocities with the “hallmarks of genocide”. 

Sixty-six MPs from across the House of Commons have joined me in writing to the foreign secretary to demand that the UK oppose her candidacy. An independent and principled UN is vital in the world. 

The job of secretary general must go to a candidate who can command the confidence of all UN member states, particularly when it comes to dealing with the war in Sudan - one of the most horrific conflicts in the world today. 

One year ago, after an 18-month siege, the city of El Fasher fell to RSF forces. At least 6,000 people were massacred in the following three days, according to a report by the UN Human Rights Office. 

Fighting alongside the RSF in El Fasher were reportedly hundreds of Colombian mercenaries trained on UAE military bases, as reported by the Financial Times and others.

Critical moment

UN investigators concluded that “individuals and entities operating from, registered in, or linked to the United Arab Emirates played a significant role in networks involved in the recruitment, financing, transportation and deployment of foreign military contractors and the provision of military-related support benefiting the Rapid Support Forces”.

The paper trail that leads from the UAE to a dead boy in Sudan
Read More »

Emirati authorities maintain blanket denials. Prominent among the deniers is Nusseibeh, who was the UAE’s representative at the UN in New York from 2013 until 2024, and later a government minister. 

In September 2024, a year before El Fasher fell, Nusseibeh wrote in a letter to the editor in the Economist: “The UAE is not providing weapons or any other support to the Rapid Support Forces or any of the warring parties in Sudan.” 

The letter followed the publication of an earlier UN report, which found “credible” allegations that the UAE was providing military support to the RSF through Chad.

For the people of Sudan, Nusseibeh is a compromised figure whose appointment would represent a partisan victory for one side in their bloody civil war.  

The secretary general of the UN is responsible for defending international peace and security - and this could not be a more critical moment for the organisation and for the world. The secretary general must be someone who is seen as an honest broker, standing up for the values of the UN, and speaking out on behalf of the vulnerable.  

Nusseibeh is not the right person for the job. I suspect the British government knows that, but will it have the courage of its convictions and oppose Nusseibeh’s candidacy?

Senior correspondent

Making today’s reset deal contingent on a further agreement on the level of tuition fees for EU citizens is designed to neutralise the leverage London gets in the next six months, EU sources have said.

Senior diplomats had already confirmed this week that the EU would defer the deal on the level of tuition fees for another six months, a move designed to give the UK leverage in parallel negotiations to have the UK included in Made in Europe legislation designed to protect EU supply chains against China.

But the move to make the food and drink deal also contingent on a tuition fees deal effectively seeks to neutralise the leverage the UK gets today.

This is a serious chess game and shows the EU, again, is willing to speak very warmly about the UK but will play absolute hard ball when it comes to conceding any points to a former member state.

It was the same point France was making last night insisting the UK could not have voting rights on legislation in relation to food and drink.

During his meeting with businesses in Brussels, PM Burnham said his EU deal would add up to 0.5% to the UK’s GDP.

“We’re pretty much there, and it’s a really good deal.”

“Treasury analysis out today is saying that now it’s clear up to 0.5% on GDP as a result of the deal. The single biggest growth intervention in this Parliament.”

US must leave West Asia and return to its own region, Iranian lawmaker says

An Iranian lawmaker said the United States must withdraw from West Asia and return to its own geographic sphere. 

Major-General Mohammad Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, told Iran’s Mehr news agency that the US could no longer confront Iran.

He said Washington had issued shifting threats, at times discussing military action on the ground and at others threatening to open the Strait of Hormuz. 

Kowsari also pointed to US threats against Iran’s nuclear programme and proposals for an economic, land, air and naval blockade of the country.

He said that Washington should leave West Asia and return to its own geographical sphere, which he said was 12,000km away.
